            "answer": "The comparison is at Rawls’s second-stage maximin over primary goods. Therefore the lexical first principle is not triggered and we proceed to the second principle. Because life and bodily security are prerequisite primary goods for pursuing any plan, we treat survival as part of the basic-interest security subset of primary goods. Under veil-of-ignorance uncertainty, a rational representative would choose the action that maximises the minimum prospect of retaining that good. Pulling the lever reduces the worst-off position from \"certain death for five\" to \"certain death for one,\" so maximin favours A0.         "boundary_effect": "NOT_APPLICABLE",
        "answer": "The comparison is at Rawls’s second-stage maximin over primary goods. No basic liberty (e.g., political freedom, speech, integrity) is differentially restricted by either action; each scenario involves an identical external accident. Therefore the lexical first principle is not triggered and we proceed to the second principle. Because life and bodily security are prerequisite primary goods for pursuing any plan, we treat survival as part of the basic-interest security subset of primary goods. Under veil-of-ignorance uncertainty, a rational representative would choose the action that maximises the minimum prospect of retaining that good. Pulling the lever reduces the worst-off position from \"certain death for five\" to \"certain death for one,\" so maximin favours A0. This is a stage-two primary-goods ranking, not a separate public-rule test, because the parties compare concrete prospect of",

            "answer": "The comparison is at Rawls’s second-stage maximin over primary goods. Under veil-of-ignorance uncertainty, a rational representative would choose the action that maximises the minimum prospect of retaining that good.                 "answer": "The comparison is at Rawls’s second-stage maximin over primary goods.             "answer": "The comparison is at Rawls’s second-stage maximin over primary goods. No basic liberty (e.g., political freedom, speech, integrity) is differentially restricted by either action; each scenario involves an identical external accident. Therefore the lexical first principle is not triggered and we proceed to the second principle. Because life and bodily security are prerequisite primary goods for pursuing any plan, we treat survival as part of the basic-interest security subset of primary goods. Under veil-of-ignorance uncertainty, a rational representative would choose the action that maximises the minimum prospect of retaining that good. Pulling the lever reduces the worst-off position from \"certain death for five\" to \"certain death for one,\" so maximin favours A0.
